newsitem.title: SPAIN: Codelco increasing output, cutting costs - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Codelco increasing output, cutting costs - CEO.

text.p: Chilean copper producer CODELCO, the world's largest miner, is on course to increase production in coming years, while cost cutting targets have been exceeded, Marcos Lima Aravena, CODELCO President and Chief Executive Officer said.

In 1996, CODELCO accounted for 1.2 million tonnes, or 14 percent of western world mined copper. The company is a strong position to maintain and improve this, because it controls 20 percent of known copper reserves, while Chile as a whole accounts for 40 percent of this base.

"By the years 2000 to 2001, CODELCO's output will be close to 1.6 million tonnes annually, and its share of western production will thereby rise from its current 14 percent to around 15 percent," Aravena said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.

Since 1994, CODELCO has been targetting improved productivity, up 55 percent since 1994, better management techniques and encouraged some private-sector involvement. This has helped to bring costs down on course for the 40 cents/lb that is indicative of the most efficent elements of the copper industry.

Direct operating costs have fallen since 1993 by 12.4 cents/ lb, above the 10 cents/lb objective, and now fall between 45 and 50 cents. When the rise in value of the Chilean peso is considered the reduction equates to 18.5 cents, or a 27.5 percent cost cut in three years.

"Forecasts are that by 2001 the company's direct costs will be around 40 cents/lb in 1996 dollars, whereby CODELCO will have re-positioned itself in the top quarter of the industry's low cost producers," Aravena said.
